statement: The universal fixed-subgroup and normalized-procyclic classification of Task A.5 remains open for arbitrary finite covers; proved families and the exact remaining comparisons are retained explicitly.
notes: All first covers, genus-one compactifications, and the entire odd and two-power dihedral families are complete. A.49 adds complete explicit families in every proper genus, including all even genera. Compact-type rational joining paths give all-prime fixed groups. A.46 gives the residue-prime normalizer criterion for potentially good p-rank-zero Jacobians. The previously displayed Y8/ell17 example is solved by A.48. Arbitrary covers outside those families, graph cycles, positive-genus joining paths, and remaining proper-homology normalizer lines still require new arguments. No cofinality or global least-index claim is made. A.50 and A.51 complete both all-prime assertions for the explicit degree27 genus10 Heisenberg cover; quaternion multiplication supplies the remaining fixed-group reduction argument. A.52 independently computes the residue3 stable components and completes both all-prime assertions for every torsion enlargement C minus q^{-1}(E[3m]), all positive m, using residue3 for odd m and residue2 for even m. A.53 supplies infinitely many all-prime fixed-inertia torsion enlargements on every occurring compactification, and conditional normalizer inheritance under further puncturing. Its open-immersion comparison is not finite refinement over the original covering map and gives no fixed-element lifting; the universal original-cover question remains Open. A.54 gives the degree125 genus51 Heisenberg cover with no CM factor in B8, all nonsplit-quartic-prime normalizers, and full pro5 fixed inertia. A.55 now completes every coefficient-prime normalizer for this genus51 cover through actual genus2 three-cusp target maps and cyclic p^n auxiliary covers with p-rank-zero Pryms. Other coefficient-prime full fixed groups remain open. No least-index claim is made. A.56 additionally settles normalizers under potential good curve reduction and special rank at least two, and for every degree-d cover at all p>d with p=1 mod4; fixed quotients remain a separate question. A.57 settles all normalizers at coefficient primes of potential good proper-curve reduction, and every degree-d cover at every p>d without congruence restrictions. Remaining normalizer cases must have p<=d and fail potential good curve reduction at all places above p, unless another proved criterion applies. Universal fixed-subgroup scope remains Open. A.58 completes the full all-prime fixed groups for the actual genus51 Heisenberg5 cover by an explicit wild compact-type model with rational cusp clusters; A.54--55 already settle its normalizers. Universal scope remains Open. A.59 completes every coefficient-prime normalizer on every finite cover with nilpotent geometric Galois closure, including nonnormal covering subgroups. Remaining universal normalizer cases are outside this entire class as well as the previously proved reduction criteria. This gives no cofinality and no full fixed-subgroup theorem for every nilpotent cover. A.60 completes both all-prime assertions for the actual Heisenberg7 degree343 genus148 cover via explicit seven-adic charts and the rational cluster of all49cusps. This exact case does not assert a cofinal family or a general fixed-group theorem for nilpotent covers. A.61 uniformly completes both all-prime assertions for every inert-prime Heisenberg cover of degreep^3 and genus1+p^2(p-1)/2. A divided differential operator proves the missing local coefficient identity; actual charts and genus exhaustion give the rational marked-tree hypothesis. This unbounded family is not claimed cofinal and does not settle all nilpotent fixed groups. A.62 completes the ordinary-prime half by actual unramified translation comparison modulo p^2 and separable-isogeny descent. Together A61/A62 now prove both assertions uniformly for the actual exponent-p Heisenberg cover at every odd primep. No cofinality or universal fixed-group conclusion follows. A63 proves all-m isogeny enlargements of every ordinary-prime Heisenberg cover, with actual noncentral component kernels supplying rational cusp companions. The universal question remains Open. A64 proves every odd Heisenberg isogeny enlargement for all m, and the general prime-outside-closure enlargement criterion, including residue2. This gives no finite refinement over the original map or fixed-element lifting. Universal TaskA5 remains Open. A65 completes every intermediate cover of every odd exponent-p Heisenberg cover, equivalently every geometric closure of exponent p and class at most two. The noncentral quotient has degree p², genus1+p(p−1)/2 and p cusps. Its actual ordinary free quotient or inert component-domination argument proves rational cusp paths directly. Universal nilpotent fixedness and TaskA5 remain Open. A66 adds every closure quotient of H_p times a prime-to-p abelian group, through actual connected elliptic-isogeny base change and copied rational cusp paths. Two nonabelian Sylow products and universal nilpotent fixedness remain outside this result. A67 adds every tetrahedral A4 closure and intermediate, using actual degree3 isogenies, a rational marked centre at3, an explicit wild C3 quotient, and the complementary elliptic factor at2. This is a non-nilpotent family, not the universal result. A68 completes both nonstable genus-seven D16 closures and all their actual intermediates by an explicit genus-two quotient, Liu residue-two invariants, eight-torsion cusp divisors and Frattini inertia. Arbitrary higher dihedral and universal covers remain outside this assertion. A69 supersedes the preceding higher-level limitation for the displayed nonstable families: every two-power m in v²=w^(2m)±6w^m+1 and every actual intermediate now satisfy both all-prime assertions. The new proof combines the ramified nilpotent tree theorem with an ordinary-Prym exclusion, actual smooth fixed-point lifting and a rooted-tree genus contradiction. No classification of all possible dihedral closures or universal TaskA5 result is asserted.

statement: For a number-field affine hyperbolic curve whose Jacobian has potentially good reduction with special p-rank zero at a place over p, every nontrivial arithmetically normalized procyclic subgroup of its geometric pro-p group is cuspidal. The proper p-adic Tate representation has no one-dimensional Qp subquotient after any finite extension.
depends_on: A.11; Brinon--Conrad Theorem5.2.1 and Proposition9.1.6; Faltings2002 Section5 Corollary4/Remarks1--5; Achter--Pries2013 Sections2.2.1/2.2.3
notes: Independent FGH conceptual audit and DE full-draft audit PASS. A rank-one crystalline isocrystal over the maximal unramified local field has an integer slope; good p-rank-zero Jacobian cohomology has all slopes strictly between0 and1. Exactness excludes every Qp rank-one subquotient, including at p=2. A.11 gives the actual rational line from a noncuspidal pro-p normalizer. No normalizer splitting or arbitrary coefficient extension is assumed.
